title: Frontier state lab
description: Choose a URL outcome to see which crawl-state transitions are allowed. Then select a node to inspect the component that owns that decision.

nodes.label: Link extractor
nodes.detail: Finds candidate links in an accepted document. Extracted links are untrusted input, not crawl work yet.

nodes.label: URL normalizer
nodes.detail: Resolves relative links, removes fragments, applies scheme and size policy, and creates the URL key used by later checks.

nodes.label: Seen URL state
nodes.detail: Combines a fast probable-repeat filter with exact durable state for important decisions and redirect aliases.

nodes.label: URL frontier
nodes.detail: Ranks admissible URLs by importance and freshness, but grants no fetch until the owning host is eligible.

nodes.label: Robots policy cache
nodes.detail: Stores fetched robots policy, expiry, path decision, and configured crawl-delay interpretation for a host.

nodes.label: Host queue
nodes.detail: Owns the host's next-allowed time and assignment lease so concurrent workers cannot bypass the crawl budget.

nodes.label: Fetch worker
nodes.detail: Uses a granted lease to perform one bounded HTTP request with redirect, timeout, and body-size limits.

nodes.label: Content processor
nodes.detail: Parses accepted content, fingerprints it, persists useful results, and emits newly discovered links back to admission.

scenarios.label: New eligible URL
scenarios.summary: A new, policy-allowed URL reaches an eligible host queue, receives one lease, and is fetched without letting parsing delay the host scheduler.
scenarios.result: The crawler makes one bounded request and feeds accepted links back through the same admission path.

scenarios.label: Known duplicate
scenarios.summary: The normalized URL already has exact seen state. It is rejected before it consumes host eligibility, a worker lease, or remote bandwidth.
scenarios.result: The URL is recorded as a duplicate decision; no fetch is scheduled.

scenarios.label: Robots blocked
scenarios.summary: The URL is new, but the cached host policy disallows its path. The frontier preserves the policy result rather than treating the URL as delayed work.
scenarios.result: The crawler does not enqueue or fetch the blocked path, protecting the remote host and avoiding needless queue growth.
